content:
The Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip launched yesterday with a pleasant surprise: its starting price is the same as the Mac Studio with the M4 Max, at $2,499.

However, if you want to upgrade the GPU, there's a catch hidden in the upgrade cost — it'll cost $300 more than what Apple's website initially shows…

This hidden upgrade cost caught John Gruber off guard while he was putting together the pricing for all the configurations of yesterday's new models.

The base configuration comes with an 18-core CPU and 32-core GPU. Apple then lists the option to upgrade to a 40-core GPU, clearly marked as requiring an additional $300.

But the catch is that selecting this option also bumps the memory from 32GB to 48GB, and the latter requires an additional $300. Since you can't upgrade the GPU cores without also upgrading to 48GB of memory, the actual upgrade cost is double the listed price — $600.

Apple only hints at this in a slightly vague way when you go to upgrade the chip.

Are you tempted to pick up the new Mac Mini or Mac Studio model? Leave a comment and let us know.
